headline: Nitto ATP Finals: Alcaraz sweeps Tiafoe 6-2, 6-2; Zverev meets Shelton in Tuesday night clash
whyCareReason: Carlos Alcaraz sweeps Frances Tiafoe 6-2, 6-2 in 69 minutes to launch Lendl Group play; Alexander Zverev faces Ben Shelton in Tuesday night's McEnroe Group battle of 1-0 unbeatens.
teaser: World No. 2 Carlos Alcaraz opens his Turin campaign with an emphatic 6-2, 6-2 win over Frances Tiafoe in 69 minutes. Daniil Medvedev tops Flavio Cobolli in two sets, while Tuesday evening features Alexander Zverev against Ben Shelton.
story:
The 2026 Nitto ATP Finals in Turin hit full stride on Monday, 16 November, as the Ivan Lendl Group delivered high-quality opening matches at Inalpi Arena.

World No. 2 Carlos Alcaraz delivered an emphatic statement of intent in the afternoon session, dismantling good friend Frances Tiafoe 6-2, 6-2 in just 69 minutes. The Spaniard fired 24 winners and never faced a break point, dominating from the baseline with devastating forehand combinations. In the evening contest, former champion Daniil Medvedev relied on clinical tiebreak execution to defeat Italian hope Flavio Cobolli 7-6 (4), 6-3.

Tuesday 17 November shifts back to the John McEnroe Group with a blockbuster evening showdown: World No. 1 Alexander Zverev faces American powerhouse Ben Shelton not before 8:30 p.m. CET in a rematch of the 2026 US Open final. Both enter at 1-0, with the winner in prime position to lock up a semi-final berth. Earlier, Arthur Fils and Rafael Jodar meet at 2:00 p.m. CET in a battle to keep semi-final hopes alive.
stakes: Alcaraz and Medvedev lead Lendl Group at 1-0; Tuesday winner between Zverev and Shelton takes sole possession of first place in McEnroe Group.
rivalryAngle: Zverev leads Shelton 6-0 in their career head-to-head series, including a four-set victory in September's US Open final at Arthur Ashe Stadium.
funFacts: Carlos Alcaraz dropped only 10 points on his serve during his 69-minute victory over Frances Tiafoe.
Alexander Zverev has won 16 of his last 18 indoor hard-court sets dating back to Vienna and Paris.
Ben Shelton struck 16 aces in his opening three-set victory over Arthur Fils on Sunday.
